objective: Break the dominant serial PWP-plus-correction service chain by overlapping a 512-bit PWP engine with a compact K4 correction engine under explicit 2/3/4-bank ownership bounds, then select the smallest useful bank depth.

selection.reason: A third bank removes another 9.45% cycle time relative to two banks, while a fourth bank adds only 1.41% speedup over three and has unmeasured storage/physical cost.
selection.bank_release: only after correction of the owning descriptor completes

interaction_finding.interpretation: Packing and overlap are complementary: packing was hidden in the serial design but becomes necessary once PWP and correction run concurrently. Ratios must come from the combined replay, not multiplication of isolated gains.

paper_safe_statement: On the frozen heldout module recurrence, three-bank bounded overlap plus one-lane K4 mask packing reduces cycles from 351,479,358 for compact256 serial service to 133,326,568, a 2.6362x same-clock module-cycle ratio; it is 1.8412x versus the current dualrow512 serial model. This is not RTL-measured, physical, full-network or system speedup.
prohibited_claims: Do not call 2.6362x full-network, end-to-end, physical or measured-frequency speedup.
Do not call 8.3619x a system result; fixed8 is a same-clock service-island baseline.
Do not multiply M140 packing and overlap ratios; use the combined exact replay only.
Do not treat the third descriptor/result bank, 512-bit macro supply, or engine duplication as free area or energy.
